paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. A decree from Caesar Augustus went out for a census (Luke 2:1), and Joseph went up to Bethlehem, the city of David (Luke 2:4). While they were there, the time came for Mary's Child to be born (Luke 2:6). So if your life feels like one long line at the registration desk, God can be at work in it.

Now look at who hears the news first. Shepherds, out in the fields at night, with the sheep and nobody else (Luke 2:8). The angel says the news is "for all the people" and that "a Savior has been born to you" (Luke 2:10-11). Jesus is Christ the Lord, and the news reached ordinary folks on the night shift, which means it's for you, too. You don't have to clean up first, friend, because the good news shows up where you are.

Then see what the shepherds do with it. They hurry off to see (Luke 2:15-16), they spread the message (Luke 2:17), and they return "glorifying and praising God" (Luke 2:20). Mary does something different and just as good: she "treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart" (Luke 2:19). So when God's Word reaches you, you can run and tell somebody, or you can sit quietly and let it sink in deep, and this story still has more to say.
